messages:
ara: propose we add a delegated sampler mode where edge proxies make sampling decisions & return a telemetry token to the central plane. reasoning: reduce RTTs and keep high-throughput routes cheap. thoughts?

mike: curious — how do we keep PII redaction/legal guarantees if decision moves to edge? auditability is main concern for enterprise customers.

sam: +1 on auditability concern. we need deterministic decision provenance and ability to re-evaluate sampled items if compliance asks. delegation is OK only if we attach strong provenance metadata and signed decisions.

jen: from console/UX side, want to avoid 20 tiny toggles. can we expose a single "delegated sampling" toggle and then a per-route override table? also need rollout UX for canarying.

ara: rough config idea I sketched:
```yaml
sampling:
  mode: delegated  # delegated | central
  decision_endpoint: https://sampler.internal/redwood/v1/decide
  default_rate: 0.01
  route_overrides:
    /v1/chat: 0.02
    /v1/embeddings: 0.2
```
this keeps the contract minimal: edge hits decision endpoint (local cache) or uses local policy when offline.

mike: ok but two big asks: 1) signed decision blob with (route, seed, policy_id, timestamp) so central can verify. 2) fallback to central decision when edge can't reach signer service.

sam: and we need to ensure the decision blob includes a redaction-level score or tag: e.g., pii_suspect: true/false, redact_profile: high/low. that way downstream reprocessing knows how to handle.

ara: agreed. example token payload I imagined: `{policy_id: "p-12", seed: 12345, sampled: true, redact_profile: "partial", sig: "..."}` — we can base64 + sig.

data-pipeline: note: if edge signs decisions, central ETL must still record the raw provenance for audits. our pipeline expects a stable schema. can we reuse existing telemetry fields instead of new ad-hoc ones?

jen: about console: rollout flow suggestion — "start delegated" button that opens a canary slider (routes + percent) and shows expected token volume & cost delta. preview should call a simulator endpoint to estimate billing.

ops-oncall: ops worry: if delegated sampler misbehaves we could accidentally sample PII at higher rate. need an emergency kill switch (global rate cap + per-route hard limits) that the console can flip immediately. also alerting when sample distribution diverges from expected.

mike: propose this enforcement: edges must set sampled=true only if proof.sig verifies with our key AND sampler_cert not older than 5m. central policy enforcer rejects anything signed by stale cert.

sam: legal asks for a retention lifecycle for signed blobs and sampled payload pointers. e.g., keep provenance for 90 days, pointers to replay data for 30 days. add that to the API contract.

ara: open question: should decision be synchronous (edge calls decision endpoint on each request) or async with a small local cache + bloom filter? sync has clearer provenance; cache reduces latency. leaning cache + short TTL.

mike: short TTL (<=30s) ok, but must include policy_version in token so we can backfill properly when policy changes.

jen: UX note: when policy_version changes, console should surface a "policy diff" and warn about changed sample counts.

data-pipeline: operational concern: if edges flood central /decide we need quota enforcement. suggest per-edge token bucket and a circuit-breaker that flips edges to local-only mode when threshold hit.

ara: action items: 1) mike + sam draft token schema + signing spec, 2) eng-platform implements /decide lightweight service + cert rotation, 3) jen prototypes console canary slider + kill switch CTA, 4) data-pipeline defines retention schema. will sync tomorrow 10am.

deploy-bot: canary deploy started for sampler-service v0.19 -> staging (commit ab12f3). :rocket:

ops-oncall: noted — will add alerts for sample-rate drift, signer failures, and edge fallback events.

jen: I'll mock the UX and share screenshots before the sync.

ara: thanks everyone. if nobody objects I’ll open a tracking RFC and a small spike ticket for the TTL cache experiment.
